questions.question: Describe the arrangement and movement of particles in a solid, a liquid and a gas, and name three ways to separate mixtures.
questions.expected_answer: In a solid, particles are packed closely in a regular pattern and vibrate on the spot. In a liquid, they are close but slide past each other. In a gas, they are far apart and move fast in all directions. Mixtures can be separated by hand sorting, sieving, settling, decanting and filtering.

questions.question: Explain what happens when salt dissolves in water, and how the salt can be recovered. What makes dissolving faster?
questions.expected_answer: Water particles pull the salt particles away and they spread evenly between the water particles, forming a clear, uniform solution; the salt is the solute and the water is the solvent. The salt is still there, as its mass shows, and it can be recovered by evaporating the water. Dissolving is faster in hot water, with stirring or shaking, and when the solute is in smaller pieces.

questions.question: Name the three kinds of water pollution, and describe how water is made safe to drink.
questions.expected_answer: Water can be polluted by insoluble substances like plastic, oil and mud; soluble substances like fertilisers, poisons and detergents; and germs from sewage, which cause water-borne illnesses. To make it safe, dirt is removed by sieving, settling, decanting and filtering, and then germs are killed by boiling or adding the right amount of bleach or chlorine. Municipal works clean water before it reaches our taps and clean wastewater before it returns to the river.
